Background:
The item for consideration is an Ordinance. Annexation of County pockets is a 2022 City
Council priority. A “County pocket” is an area of unincorporated land 100% surrounded by
the City of Cheyenne. A related “Assigned Zoning” pursuant to Unified Development Code
(UDC) Section 2.2.8 ordinance is also on the agenda.
The proposed Governing Body review schedule is as follows:
• Introduction and Referral  February 9, 2026
• Public Services Committee  February 17, 2026
• Second reading    February 23, 2026
• Public Services Committee  March 2, 2026
• Third and final reading   March 9, 2026

[2026-03-09 March | City Council | doc] This annexation is comprised of 16 properties 100% surrounded by the City (See attached
map). Of the 16 parcels, most are developed with residential uses, one is a farm, and others
are developed with commercial or industrial uses. The City has maintained contact with the
County Planning Office to coordinate any pending permits or development reviews.
Currently there are no active permits or development specific to the properties proposed for
annexation.
On December 2, 2025, City staff mailed a courtesy notice by first class mail to all landowners
included in this annexation area inviting them to a “Question and Answer” on Tuesday
December 16, 2025. During the meeting staff provided information regarding trash
collection, water and sewer services, continuation of uses and what to expect with the
annexation. Only one resident attended the meeting. Their main concern was about their
farm/farm stand and the continuation of the use once annexed. Staff is proposing that their

[2026-03-09 March | City Council | doc] property be assigned the AG Agricultural zone which will allow the farm to continue as a use
by right and would not change the use of the property.
The existing use of any property annexed, including any livestock use, will be allowed to
continue as is as a nonconforming use.  Nonconforming uses may continue until they are
abandoned for a period of 12-months. Residents within pockets have been encouraged to
complete a Land Use Documentation form detailing the existing use of the land for
documentation purposes. The form is simply a tool to assist future City staff members to
determine if a use was in existence at the time of annexation.

[2026-03-09 March | City Council | doc] City-initiated annexations do not require an owner’s signature. To initiate an annexation, the
City must adopt a resolution certifying that the annexation complies with Wyoming State
Statute § 15-1-402. After the City adopts this resolution, the annexation follows the typical
schedule, including a public hearing and the approval of an Ordinance which annexes the
land. The Governing Body adopted Resolution No. 6511 initiating this annexation on January
26, 2025.
As with any annexation, City services will be extended to service the land contained in the
annexation. City utilities are already located in the vicinity. Police, fire, and sanitation services
will be provided. Infrastructure improvements required related to the annexation are minimal.
Future development such as subdivision or new development will require on- and off-site
infrastructure improvements. Existing infrastructure will remain as is upon annexation.

[2026-03-09 March | City Council | doc] The areas proposed for annexation are adjacent to land under City jurisdiction. Development
in this area is a natural extension of the City. 100 % of the perimeter of the annexation area is
contiguous to City limits.
Due to meeting the review criteria found in Wyoming Statute § 15-1-402 and the annexation
conforming with the 2022 City Council goal to annex County pockets, staff recommends
approval of this annexation.
Staff Recommendation:
Staff recommends the Governing Body approve the Annexation Ordinance.

[2026-03-09 March | City Council | doc] Responses to questions of David Kniseley regarding WYfresh Farms regarding the affects of annexation.
Stormwater Fee
The estimated stormwater fee is approximately $38.00 per month, based on impervious surface
calculations. The fee is assessed at $0.0024 per square foot. A link to the stormwater fee map and
Engineering Department contact information has been provided to him if he has questions or concerns.
Property Taxes
The estimated annual tax increase is $203.80. The County Assessor may reassess the property upon
annexation. The Assessor's contact information has been provided to him to obtain additional
information.
Drainage
The Planning and Development Department is not aware of any current drainage projects affecting the
property. Engineering Department contact information has been provided to the inquirer o him to
obtain additional information.
Use of Land for Livestock
The property is proposed to be zoned Agricultural (AG), which permits livestock. Minor adjustments in

[2026-03-09 March | City Council | doc] animal numbers within existing pastures do not require approval. Expansion of livestock use areas
requires site plan review. Rotating or designated animal areas should be documented using a Land Use
Documentation Form and a web link to that form has been provided to him.
Right to Farm and Ranch Act
The Act generally protects agricultural operations from nuisance claims when standard management
practices are followed. It does not exempt property owners from compliance with local regulations.
Expansion of Farming or Livestock Areas
Expanding the area used for farming or livestock requires submission of a site plan. Infrastructure
improvements may be considered but are evaluated in proportion to the scope of the proposed
expansion.
Guard Dog Vaccinations
Vaccination requirements apply within both City and County jurisdictions. Animal Control contact
information has been provided to him to obtain additional information..
Farmstand Licensing

[2026-03-09 March | City Council | doc] A $75 annual license is required for operation of a mobile food cart, along with compliance with public
health requirements. City Clerk's Office contact information has been provided to him if he desires
further information.
Discharge of Firearms and Livestock Protection
Discharge of firearms within the City is prohibited except at designated ranges. Alternative wildlife and
nuisance animal control measures are available. Contact information for the police department and the
Wyoming State Game and Fish Department has been provided to him for alternatives.
Jefferson/Walterscheid Intersection
Engineering staff have been notified of visibility and signage concerns at this intersection. Additional
signage is anticipated to address traffic movement restrictions after annexation.

[2026-03-09 March | City Council | doc] Building Permits
Existing structures will be recognized as constructed and are not required to be upgraded. New
structures, including hoop houses, will require permits. Property owners are encouraged to document
existing structures prior to ordinance adoption.
Land Use and Agricultural Operations
Annexation will not require the discontinuation of agricultural operations, livestock activities, farmstand
operations, or existing driveways. Current uses may continue under the proposed zoning.

The current use of the property is a residence and an urban farm with a farm stand. These uses would

District, and SS – Support Services. The AD and SS zones are special purpose zones and not applicable
to this area.

administrative, or requires conditional use approval. This is the most flexible zone for agricultural uses
and would allow the farm and farmstand to continue operations.

ORDINANCE NO. __________
ENTITLED: “AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION  13.20.050, GENERAL
PROHIBITIONS, AND SECTION 13.20.070, LOCAL LIMITS , OF
CHAPTER 13.20 , WASTEWATER TREATMENT AND DISPOSAL , OF
THE CODE OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE, WYOMING , TO REVISE
LOCAL DISCHARGE LIMITS AND RELATED PROVISIONS IN
COMPLIANCE WITH NPDES AND WPDES PERMIT REQUIREMENTS.”
BE IT ORDAINED BY THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE,
WYOMING:
Section 1.  The Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne finds and declares that:
A. State and federal wastewater discharge permitting regulations require that publicly
owned treatment works (POTWs) provide a written technical evaluation of the need to revise local
limits following the issuance or reissuance of a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System
(NPDES) permit;
B. On February 20, 2024, the State of Wyoming issued permits authorizing the
discharge of treated wastewater from  the Dry Creek Water Reclamation Facility and the Crow

[2026-04-27 April | City Council | doc] Creek Water Reclamation Facility to receiving waters identified as Crow Creek, South Platte River
Basin, in accordance with the requirements of the Wyoming Pollution Discharge Elimination
System (WPDES) Permits WY0022934 and WY0022381, respectively;
C. In compliance with the NPDES permitting requirements , the City of Cheyenne
Board of Public Utilities (BOPU) submitted a proposed Sampling Plan for  review by the
Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) on January 22, 2025, and the EPA approved the
Sampling Plan on June 2, 2025;
D. In compliance with the NPDES permitting requirements , BOPU  submitted a
proposed Pollutants of Concern (POCs) report for EPA review on  May 29, 2025 , providing
information pertaining to the screening and evaluation of pollutants and  the proposed final
determination of POCs to be included in the Local Limits Evaluation, and the EPA agreed with
the POCs Evaluation on June 2, 2025;
E. In compliance with the NPDES permitting requirements, BOPU  submitted a

[2026-04-27 April | City Council | doc] proposed technically based Local Limits Evaluation for EPA review on August 6, 2025, and the
EPA deemed the proposed local limitations approvable on January 28, 2026; and
F. To remain in compliance with the NPDES permitting requirements, to preserve the
quality of Crow Creek, to maintain the plant at the highest performance levels, to protect the plant’s
operating staff, and to protect the overall environment of the South Platte River Basin, the
Governing Body determines  that it is necessary and appropriate to amend certain wastewater
treatment and disposal provisions of the Cheyenne Municipal Code as provided in this Ordinance.

Chapter 13.20, Wastewater Treatment and Disposal , of Title 13, Public Services, of the code of
the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming, are amended to read:
13.20.050 - General prohibitions.
A. No industrial user shall contribute or cause to be contributed, directly or indirectly, to the
POTW any pollutant or wastewater which will pass through or cause interference with the
operation or performance of the POTW. These general prohibitions and the specific
prohibitions in subsection B of this section shall apply to all the industrial users of the
POTW, whether or not they are subject to pretreatment standards or requirements.
B. Specific Prohibitions. No industrial user shall contribute the following substances to the
POTW:
1. Any substances which by reason of their nature or quantity will create a fire or
explosion hazard or be injurious to the POTW or to the operation of the POTW,

[2026-04-27 April | City Council | doc] capable of causing damage or hazard to structures, equipment or personnel of the
POTW;
6. Any substance which may cause a public nuisance, cause hazard to life or prevent entry
into the sewers for maintenance and repair;
7. Heated substances in amounts which will prevent entry into the sewer system of
authorized personnel or will inhibit biological activity in the POTW resulting in
interference, but in no case heat in such quantities that the temperature at the POTW
treatment plant exceeds one hundred four (104) degrees Fahrenheit or forty (40)
degrees Celsius. A limit may be required in particular situations where the temperature
has caused or has potential to cause pass through of an interceptor, pass through or
interference in the POTW;

[2026-04-27 April | City Council | doc] may create an explosion hazard or in any way have a deleter ious effect to the POTW or
constitute a nuisance or a hazard to POTW personnel, the general public, the environment,
or the receiving stream shall be prohibited.

amendment to the ordinance treating the authority, redescribe the development area so as to
include the additional property as described in the petition. From the eﬀective date of the
amendment the additional property shall be included within the development area and shall be
subject to any taxes thereafter imposed by the municipality for the use and beneﬁt of the
authority.”

RECOMMENDED MOTION:
Should the associated Future Land Use Map Amendment be recommended for approval:
Move to recommend the governing body approve the rezoning of Tract 1, H and B Tracts and Lot
2, Block 1, H and B Tracts, 2nd Filing to LI Light Industrial as shown in the attached zone change
map, noting that the project meets the review criteria for approval.
Should the associated Future Land Use Map Amendment be recommended for denial:
Move to recommend the governing body deny the rezoning of Tract 1, H and B Tracts and Lot 2,
Block 1, H and B Tracts, 2nd Filing to LI Light Industrial as shown in the attached zone change map,
noting that the project does not meet review criteria 1, 2, and 8 – the LI zoning request being

BACKGROUND:

[2026-04-27 April | City Council | doc] This zone change application proposes changing the zoning from County LI Light Industrial, AG Agricultural,
and AR Agricultural Residential to LI Light Industrial for roughly 90 acres of land. The land is currently occupied
by a tree nursery, rural residential development, and vacant land Outside of this application, discussion has
occurred regarding development of a campground or recreational vehicle park; however, those intentions have
not been formally stated. Campground and Recreational Vehicle Park land uses can be accommodated via
conditional use process in the existing zone districts.
The application has been submitted concurrently with a proposed future land use map amendment to
change the subject property to Mixed-use Employment. Staff’s discussion and recommendation on the
proposed future land use map amendment are found in that application’s staff report.
The northernmost portion of land was annexed in 2015 and proposed to be platted as “Heiduck Addition”. The

[2026-04-27 April | City Council | doc] proposed zoning with the annexation and the plat was City LI Light Industrial. The underlying County zone was
County LI and the City LI zone would be analogous to the County zone. There were some issues with the
project that required corrective ordinances months later, and the plat never ended up getting recorded.
Unfortunately, the Ordinance for the City zone was tied to the recording of the plat, not the recording of the
annexation. The property still technically has not been given a City zone. However, as the original intent of the
Council at time of annexation was LI zoning, and as representation on the zoning map for the City and County
LI zones are identical, this property has been treated as zoned LI by previous staff. This zone change includes LI
zoning for the northernmost parcel to clean-up the past issue. Should this zoning request zoning fail, staff will
run a corrective ordinance for the northern area currently County LI.

of those present and voting may approve or disapprove official business. The Chair shall not vote

[2026-04-27 April | City Council | doc] as a member of the Planning Commission unless a tie vote occurs of the majority present and
voting.” (emphasis added)

Subject: Downtown Development Authority Proposed Budget - Fiscal Year 2027

Background:
Attached is the proposed budget for fiscal year 2027 (July 1 to June 30). The proposed Governing Body
review schedule is as follows:
• Introduction and Referral: April 27, 2026
• Finance Committee: May 5, 2026
• Final consideration: May 11, 2026
The budget represents a $14,610.00 increase in mill levy assessment collections ($501,610.00) and a
decrease in interest earned (-$27,759.15). The interest earned estimate is based on an estimated
$625,000 dollars being left in the Wyoming Government Investment Fund (WGIF) which as of April 7,
2026, has a seven-day yield of 3.56% (versus $1 million in the WGIF account during FY2026).
The proposed budget of $1,052,800 is $226,526 more than fiscal year 2026 (per the final FY26 budget

[2026-04-27 April | City Council | doc] increase in April 2026), brings in $464,190 from reserves, accounts for a $30,000 grant from the
Cheyenne-Laramie Co. Economic Development Joint Powers Board, and $10,000 in funding from
Laramie County. The City contributes approximately $290,900 covering all payroll, insurance, and
benefits for employees. Additionally, other City staff provide support to DDA employees at no cost to
the DDA. The FY2027 Proposed Budget includes costs associated with an independent office outside of

paratransit/on-demand service for the public. The modification wud renew on an annual basis at
a 5% increase each year.
The current contract amount is $54,525.00 (annually with a 5% increase). The addition of the
Spare Fixed Route Platform and one time implementation fee at $78,000.00, for a grand total of
$134,711.00

Consideration of Bid #E-4-25 for the purchase (3) Fire Apparatus for the City of Cheyenne,
Cheyenne Fire Rescue Department (CFR), funded by Future Ballot Specific Purpose Option Tax
Fund, was approved by the Governing Body on November 25, 2024. At the time of placing the
order, the anticipated delivery timeframe was three to four years out.

Under Cab  PUC, Type 1 Pumper) and is considered operationally equivalent for the purposes
intended under the bid.
After review, CFR has determined that the opportunity to take delivery of a substantially similar

Section 1.  Definitions.
EMPLOYEE/EMPLOYEES – As used in this ordinance,  “employee” or “employees”
means sworn police officers below the rank of chief.
Section 2.  Applicability.
The terms and conditions of employment as set forth herein shall apply to all employees as
defined herein.
Section 3.  Purpose.
The purpose of this ordinance is to define the terms and conditions of employment for
employees. The rights contained herein are in addition to any rights an employee may have under
the Cheyenne Police Department Policy Manual (as that document may be amended at any time,
before or after passage of this ordinance), and applicable federal, state, and local laws. In areas of

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] conflict between this ordinance and established federal, state, or local laws, the latter shall govern.
This ordinance comprises the exc lusive statement of employee terms and conditions of
employment. Any other agreement with or representation made to any employee by a supervisor,
agent or officer of the City of Cheyenne which is in conflict with or in addition to this ordinance
is specifically disclaimed by the City of Cheyenne, except for the Cheyenne  Police Department
Policy Manual and except for agreements entered into by and between supervisory personnel and
employees establishing specific job expectations, requirements or discipline which are part of the
employee’s official personnel file maintained by the Human Resources Department.
Section 4.  Cheyenne Police Department Policy Manual and Benefits Policy.
The Cheyenne Police Department Policy Manual, including the benefit policy set forth in
Exhibit A as it exists or is amended from time to time, are incorporated herein and made part of

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] these terms and conditions of employment and shall apply only to sworn police officers.
Section 5.  Compensation.
The compensation paid to employees is set forth in Exhibit B , which is  attached and
incorporated by reference. The compensation appropriate for the aforementioned employees shall
be computed with reference to the assigned grade of the individual employee.  Placement within

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] the appropriate grade under the new plan will be determined a case-by-case basis, based upon
employee’s hire date or promotion date, by the Chief in consultation with  the Director of the
Human Resources Department. The Governing Body for the City of Cheyenne reserves the right,
in its sole discretion, to modify or change pay scales. Employees will receive, in addition to basic
pay, specialty on-call pay as set forth in Exhibit C, which is attached hereto and incorporated by
reference. Employees will receive, in addition to basic pay, longevity pay as set forth in Exhibit
D, attached hereto and incorporated by reference.
For any employee called to active military duty, the City of Cheyenne will compensate the
difference between the employee’s City base pay and total military monetary compensation
(commonly listed on the military leave and earnings statement as the total entitlements), provided
the military compensation is lower than the City base pay. Base pay is defined as the regular pay

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] the employee would have received from the City had they not been called to active military duty ,
not including on-call or specialty pay.
Section 6.  Continuation of Employment.
Any employee covered by this ordinance who continues his or her term of employment
during and beyond the term of this ordinance shall be entitled to advancement annually (subject to
the provisions of Section 5), as set forth in Exhibit B, upon recommendati on of the employee’s
supervisor, if the mayor and council approve funds to pay the increases.
Section 7.  Health, Medical, Dental, and Life.
Each employee who participates in the city health insurance program shall contribute ten
percent (10%) of the monthly premium based on the coverage level they select. This contribution
will be made through payroll deduction.
For Fiscal Year 2027, the City will continue to cover ninety percent (90%) of the health
insurance premium for employees who complete d the 2025–2026 Wellness Program by June 30,

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] 2026. Employees who chose not to participate in the Wellness Program will receive an eighty-five
percent (85%) contribution from the City and will be responsible for the remaining fifteen percent
(15%) of the premium.
The City will maintain dental insurance for employees pursuant to the dental plan, a copy
of which is  on file with the Human Resources Department.  The City will pay premiums for
employees. If an employee wishes to maintain dental insurance under this plan for eligible
dependents as defined in Appendix B of the dental plan, he or she may do so by paying the
premium for the additional person(s) insured.
The City will pay premiums for term life insurance on all employees in accordance with
the term life insurance plan on file in the Human Resources Department and City Clerk’s Office.

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] Section 8.  Term.
The terms and conditions of employment set forth in this ordinance shall be effective as of
the City’s July 2026 payroll. This ordinance will terminate upon passage of a replacement
ordinance.
Section 9.  Repeal of Other Ordinances.
All other ordinances establishing specific terms and conditions of employment are

If any clause, sentence, paragraph, or part of this ordinance or application to any person or
circumstance shall for any reason be adjudged by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid,
such judgment shall not affect, impair, or invalidate the remainder of this agreement.
Section 11 .  This ordinance shall be in full force and effect upon its passage and
publication.

EMPLOYEE WAGE AND BENEFIT POLICY
THIS POLICY COVERS ALL COMMISSIONED OFFICERS OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE
POLICE DEPARTMENT.
1. MONTHLY WAGES.
a. Wages.
All commissioned officers are covered by the City of Cheyenne pay plan.
All step increases shall be on the officer’s original date of employment or promotion date.
b. Lateral Transfer Program.
Lateral entry candidates must be currently certified as a Wyoming peace officer or in a
state with a reciprocity agreement with Wyoming.  If not currently certified in Wyoming, lateral
entry candidates must take and pass the Wyoming POST challenge test, as well as the Wyoming
criminal law and domestic violence courses offered through the Wyoming Law Enforcement
Academy.
Subject to these requirements, the department offers a lateral transfer program for officers
with prior qualifying law enforcement experience. At the chief’s discretion, qualified officers will
be placed in the step program according to their experience as follows upon date of hire:

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] 2 to 4 years of experience: Grade 201 - Step 3
4 to 6 years of experience: Grade 201 - Step 4
6 + years of experience: Grade 201 - Step 5
c. Specialty On Call Pay.
Eligible employees will be entitled to receive specialty on-call pay. Employees are limited
to receiving compensation for a maximum of two (2) specialties per month.
An eligible employee is one who serves as a first-line supervisor (field training officer) or
is required to be available for callout and does not receive any other compensation for being on
call.
d. Longevity Pay.
Eligible employees will be entitled to receive longevity pay based on years of service.
Longevity raises will be effective on the employee’s anniversary month.

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] 2
2. OVERTIME.
a. Patrol Officers and Patrol Sergeants.
All sergeants and officers who are called in for overtime duties will receive a minimum of
two and one-half (2.5) hours of overtime pay, excepting court appearances , which are limited to
two (2) hours of overtime pay or compensatory time if the time spent is two (2) hours or less. All
court time in excess of two (2) hours is to be paid at time and one -half the classification rate. All
patrol officers and patrol sergeants shall be limited to eighty (80) hours of accumulated
compensatory time, at which time,  they must take paid overtime until they reduce their
compensatory time below the eighty (80) hour level.
All officers assigned to acting  sergeant duties will be compensated two (2) hours of
overtime for each shift. All sergeants assigned acting lieutenant duties will be compensated one -
hour straight time for each shift.
Should the acting sergeant, lieutenant , or captain duties extend beyond thirty consecutive

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] days, the department may temporarily promote the employee  and place the employee in the
appropriate pay grade of the new position.
3. HOLIDAYS.
The officers and sergeants of the City of Cheyenne Police Department will be entitled to
those paid holidays that are set by Personnel Rules and Regulations of the City of Cheyenne, as
amended from time to time, and as enjoyed by personnel of other depart ments of the City, to
include “Special Holidays” or other paid time off afforded to other City employees.
The rate of pay for these holidays will be computed on the basis of 2,080 hours per year.
The officer working on a holiday has the option of taking overtime pay or compensatory time at
one and one-half times the classification rate.  If the holiday falls on an officer’s regular day off,
he will be given eight (8) hours of straight pay or compensatory time. Likewise, if the holiday falls
on the officer’s vacation, or while on sick leave, the holiday will not be counted as vacation time
or sick leave.

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] 4. SICK LEAVE.
Each officer shall accumulate sick leave time at the rate of ten (10) hours for each month
of continuous employment to a maximum of 640 hours.
Officers who have completed four years of continuous service and terminate from the City
shall receive fifty percent (50%) of their accrued sick leave at their regular base rate, not to exceed
240 hours. In the case of retirement, an employee will be reimbursed fully for his or her accrued
sick time up to 240 hours. Accrual awards for the final month of employment shall be administered
in the same manner and under the same conditions as those applied to all other employees of the
City of Cheyenne.

Additional Analysis
Sunset Clause:
Enabling Language:
Section 3 of the proposed ordinance adds a new subsection c.4 to subsection d. This subsection
allows a use that was previously approved but is later reclassified as a Special Use through a

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] Code amendment, to continue operating for a period of time established by the adopting
ordinance. After that period expires, the use must obtain Special Use approval to continue
operating.
Sunset Date Defined:
Section 10 of the proposed ordinance requires compliance with these new regulations for uses
that were previously classified as “Entertainment, Amusement, Recreation Services—Other” and
as a result of the ordinance classified as “Gaming Center” by December 31, 2027. The sunset date
parallels legislation passed during the 2026 legislative budget session (Senate File 45 / Enrolled
Act 51) which allows current approvals to run through December 31, 2027, and requires the
facilities be subject to City approval after July 1, 2027. Under the legislation, local governments
may deny continued approval only upon a showing of good cause. The goal of the Special Use
approval is to compliment the licensing approval and strengthen ties to development-specific
review criteria.
Discussion on Sunset Period:

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] Financially, the scale of the existing industry also supports the reasonableness of the proposed
amortization period. Based on Wyoming’s one percent tax on gaming handle, the combined
annual handle of the existing facilities in the corporate limits of Cheyenne is estimated at
approximately $640 million (based on FY2025 budget revenue). Using a rough estimated
operator take of approximately nine percent, the facilities collectively may generate gross
gaming revenue in the range of approximately $57.6 million annually, although actual figures
may vary based on gaming volume and payout rates. Even at lower estimated take rates of six
percent, collective operator revenue would still approximate $38.4 million annually. These figures
indicate that the facilities have substantial ongoing revenue generation capacity during the
transition period. Not included in this calculation is any revenue that is dedicated to supporting
the local horse racing ecosystem like funding prize money for State horse racing tracks.

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] Significant information regarding revenue. Additional information regarding pari-mutual
wagering and historic horse racing was prepared for the 2026 Wyoming State Legislature and
that information is online here: https://wyoleg.gov/InterimCommittee/2024/02-
20240507HollandAndHart-PariMutuelWageringHHR.pdf.
Sunset periods for nonconforming uses typically consider factors such as the character of the
use, the extent of permanent investment, the portability of equipment, the time already spent in
operation, and the ability of the operator to recover investment costs. Cheyenne’s historic horse
racing facilities differ from typical nonconforming commercial uses (like an automotive shop in a
residential neighborhood) because the primary operational assets consist of electronic gaming
terminals rather than permanent physical infrastructure. Electronic gaming terminals are

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] depreciating assets, portable, and able to be moved from location to location. Staff believes this
sunset period is appropriate for gaming center uses.

A new Regional Entertainment (RE) Overlay District is proposed and extends to four areas of the
community to encourage urban and infill development and support redevelopment
opportunities in evolving and transitioning corridors within the City. Also, the designated areas
promote development that leverages proximity to regional destinations, major transportation
corridors, and interchange areas to attract visitors, support economic activity, and increase
vitality across a range of urban contexts. Attached is a map identifying the areas where the
overlay district will be established. In the event land areas are annexed and within the area
defined as being within the overlay district, they will be zoned concurrent with annexation.

Subject: DDA FY27 City Work Program MOU
Background:
The item for consideration is a Memorandum of Agreement between the City of Cheyenne and the
Cheyenne Downtown Development Authority. The purpose of the agreement is to allow the City to provide
professional and administrative services to the Downtown Development Authority (DDA) Board for the
administration of redevelopment programs and efforts in the Downtown Development District (map of the
Downtown Development District attached). The proposed Governing Body review schedule is as follows:
• Introduction and Referral: June 8, 2026
• Finance Committee: June 16, 2026
• Final Consideration: June 22, 2026
This agreement allows the City Planning and Development Department to provide professional and

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] administrative services to the DDA Board in carrying out its goals. The DDA Executive Director will serve as
the primary contact for the DDA. The Board of Directors, alongside the Director of Planning and
Development, shall hire employees (including the DDA Staff) to implement the DDA Board’s vision as set in
adopted plans. DDA Staff members will be City employees with City benefits yet shall act only under the
authority of the DDA Board and not under the direction of the City or any of its departments.
This agreement is modeled after a prior 1991 agreement (Contract No. 2891), the 2023 agreement
(Contract No. 7704), and the current 2025 agreement (Contract No. 8188), all of which allowed the City to
provide professional and administrative services to the DDA Board.
The agreement allows $283,513, if available, of the mill levy to support the FY26 goals of the DDA program
instead of towards administrative and personnel expenses. The estimated 2026 mill levy revenue is

[2026-06-23 June | City Council | doc] $501,610. This redirect will support event sponsorships, beautification efforts, grant programs, and other
operations necessary to provide DDA services, while ensuring compliance with regulating state statutes
and the state Constitution. The City has previously committed general fund money to the DDA and will
direct funding to support this operation as well.
The agreement is valid for one fiscal year (per Section 2.76.060 (Professional and administrative support)
of the Code of the City of Cheyenne, Wyoming) and will need to be reconsidered prior to expiration on
June 30, 2027. Presently the DDA is staffed through City via the Planning and Development Department.
The current MOU between the City and the DDA terminates on June 30, 2026.
